results.explanation: At the declared notes POST entry, PaperlessNotePermissions is the configured permission class. Its POST global check requires add_note, view_document, and change_document, and the premises state that all are present, so that global check is satisfied. The handler then performs a separate owner-aware view_document check on the target document; the premises state that the caller has object view access, so this check is satisfied. In the POST branch, before any creation, the handler performs a separate owner-aware change_document check on the same document. Because the caller is not the owner and lacks the object change_document grant, the supplied owner-aware implementation does not authorize that check, and the handler returns HTTP 403. Note.objects.create is therefore a protected side effect that is not reached in this scenario; it would create the note only after the change check passes. The fixed source supports a deny at this declared-entry boundary. No repository-wide or deployment-level completeness claim is made.

entry.statement: The notes action is a detail action accepting POST and is configured with PaperlessNotePermissions.

binding.statement: The owner-aware permission helper permits an owner or an unowned object, otherwise requiring the supplied object permission through the permission checker.

citations.quote:
def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)

control.statement: The POST branch separately applies the owner-aware change_document check to the target document and returns forbidden when it fails.
For POST, PaperlessNotePermissions checks the global add_note, view_document, and change_document permissions, and calls request.user.has_perms for them.
The handler checks owner-aware view_document access on the loaded target document and returns forbidden if that check fails.

effect.statement: Note.objects.create is the note-creation side effect, using the target document, request note data, and current user, but it occurs only after the preceding change check.

condition.statement: Under the premises, the caller is a different user from the document owner and has no object change_document grant, so the owner-aware change_document check is unsatisfied.

facts.statement: The notes action is a detail action accepting POST and is configured with PaperlessNotePermissions.
For POST, PaperlessNotePermissions checks the global add_note, view_document, and change_document permissions, and calls request.user.has_perms for them.
The handler checks owner-aware view_document access on the loaded target document and returns forbidden if that check fails.
The owner-aware permission helper permits an owner or an unowned object, otherwise requiring the supplied object permission through the permission checker.
The POST branch separately applies the owner-aware change_document check to the target document and returns forbidden when it fails.
Under the premises, the caller is a different user from the document owner and has no object change_document grant, so the owner-aware change_document check is unsatisfied.
